categoryNote: Storage category. Component-store cleanup is NX16-009 (DISM /ResetBase is rejected, r5); SysMain configuration is NX11-009; search indexing scope is NX01-009; plan-level power settings (disk idle timeouts, sleep/hibernate) are NX09. NX06 owns storage inventory, NTFS behavior (fsutil), drive maintenance scheduling, documented Storage Sense policy, on-demand cleanup operations, the storage-stack D3 policy and drive health reporting. No performance claims anywhere: verification answers whether the recorded configuration holds.

tweaks.name: Storage inventory & SSD/HDD/NVMe classification
tweaks.description: Read-only physical-disk and volume inventory with an explicit media/bus classification that every storage-conditional NEXTRIX decision consumes.
tweaks.objective: Establish what storage the machine actually has before any storage tweak is judged applicable.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxStorageInventory reads documented properties only: Get-PhysicalDisk (MediaType, BusType, Size, HealthStatus, OperationalStatus), Get-Disk (IsBoot, IsSystem, PartitionStyle) and Get-Volume (file system, size, free space). Classification is explicit and never guessed: nvme-ssd, ssd, scm, hdd, usb, unknown; a MediaType of Unspecified stays 'unknown' instead of being rounded down to 'not an SSD'. trimApplicable is derived from the media class only, because rotational devices ignore unmap/trim (fsutil behavior documentation). Uncertainty is a first-class field: when Get-PhysicalDisk fails, readSucceeded is false and the report states that the storage class is unknown rather than inventing a type. NxHardware keeps a coarse hasSsd/hasHdd summary for the eligibility resolver; this entry is the deep per-disk/per-volume report and the source of the detail NX06-002 (TRIM) and NX06-012 (D3) consume. No writes, no journal entries, no scheduled task.
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX storage report; each consumer infers storage class ad hoc.
tweaks.proposedState: A per-disk/per-volume report with classification, trim/applicability flags, health status and explicit uncertainty notes.

verify.procedure: Report has readSucceeded=true and at least one physical disk, or readSucceeded=false with the reason in uncertainty. Every disk carries mediaType, busType, classification, trimApplicable and a volume list; classification matches Get-PhysicalDisk on re-read.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only diagnostic; nothing is journaled or changed.

documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/storage/get-physicaldisk (MediaType/BusType/HealthStatus; fetched 2026-11-23)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/fsutil-behavior (rotational media and trim/unmap semantics)
src/nxcore/NxHardware.ps1 Get-NxStorageReport (coarse eligibility summary; this entry is the deep report)

tweaks.name: TRIM enable & verification
tweaks.description: Ensures NTFS delete notification (TRIM/unmap) is enabled, with the exact prior fsutil state and registry presence journaled.
tweaks.objective: Restore the documented Windows default (TRIM enabled) when a machine is found with delete notification disabled.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxTrimEnabled checks storage class first: with no SSD/SCM media the entry skips with a reason, because rotational devices ignore trim and disabling it on an HDD (the SapphireOS SSD/HDD .reg pair, r3) has no documented benefit - that pattern is deliberately not adopted. Capture records the raw fsutil behavior query disabledeletenotify output, the parsed NTFS and ReFS values, and the observed persistence value (NtfsDisableDeleteNotify) so presence and absence are both restorable. Apply runs the documented command fsutil behavior set disabledeletenotify 0; verification re-queries and requires the NTFS line to report TRIM allowed (no restart is required - documented). A failed verification restores the exact original (registry value first, fsutil only if the semantic still differs) and journals 'failed'. NX06 never touches ReFS v2 mapper values. Journal target type is 'fsutilBehavior', so rollback is delegated to Invoke-Nx06Rollback; ReviOS/Sapphire references are configuration precedents only, and no performance outcome is claimed.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: NTFS delete notification enabled (value normally absent).
tweaks.proposedState: NTFS DisableDeleteNotify parsed as 0 (TRIM allowed) with the original state journaled.

verify.procedure: fsutil behavior query disabledeletenotify re-parses to 'TrimEnabled' for NTFS; the registry presence/value is recorded in the verify entry. Only-if-ours rollback compares the live parsed value with the recorded modified value.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx06Rollback -TweakId NX06-002 rewrites the journaled registry presence exactly (deleting the value when it did not exist before) and re-aligns the fsutil semantic only when the registry restore did not reproduce it. A value changed after apply is reported diverged, never clobbered.

originalState.method: Raw fsutil behavior query disabledeletenotify output (NTFS + ReFS lines), parsed values and the persistence registry descriptor captured BEFORE any change; unparseable output refuses the mutation.

sideEffects: None expected: enabling delete notification is the Windows default. Microsoft documents that some specific devices can degrade with delete notification enabled; rollback restores the exact prior state.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/fsutil-behavior (disabledeletenotify semantics, no restart required; fetched 2026-11-23)
research/sources/r3-sapphire-vain.md (SSD/HDD .reg pair with opposite TRIM values - reference only, rejected for HDD)

tweaks.name: Optimize Drives schedule configuration
tweaks.description: Configures the Windows Optimize Drives maintenance schedule (weekly/monthly) and optionally re-enables the task; never disables it, and journals the full task XML.
tweaks.objective: Keep Windows' own volume optimize/retrim maintenance scheduled and explicit instead of disabling it (the reference-project pattern).
tweaks.technicalExplanation: On Windows 11 the Optimize Drives task (\Microsoft\Windows\Defrag\ScheduledDefrag) is a maintenance task: MaintenanceSettings Period/Deadline with no triggers, plus an Enabled flag. Set-NxOptimizeDrivesSchedule captures the task state, the maintenance period/deadline, trigger count, action command and the complete task XML, then applies only MaintenanceSettings.Period/Deadline (P7D weekly or P1M monthly) through Set-ScheduledTask -Settings on the live task object; Settings.Enabled is changed only when the owner passes -EnableTask. Triggers, actions, principal and every other setting are untouched, and the entry never disables the task, never deletes it and never invents a trigger-based schedule: a task without MaintenanceSettings is reported and skipped. Verification re-reads period, deadline and enabled state. Rollback compares the live schedule with the journaled modified values (only-if-ours) and re-registers the exact journaled XML; divergence is reported, never overwritten. Reference context: SapphireOS disables ScheduledDefrag (r3 line 367) and ReviOS' revert ledger records defrag breakage after unrelated service changes (r2) - this entry is the inversion, with no performance claim.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: Optimize Drives maintenance task with Period P7D and Deadline P1M (disabled on some images and VMs).
tweaks.proposedState: Task enabled (when requested) with the documented maintenance period/deadline; full prior XML journaled.

verify.procedure: Get-ScheduledTask re-read returns the requested MaintenanceSettings Period and Deadline (and Enabled when requested); last run time/result are reported as context. Trigger-based tasks are skipped instead of rewritten.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx06Rollback -TweakId NX06-003 verifies the live schedule still equals the recorded modified values (only-if-ours) and re-registers the journaled original XML with Register-ScheduledTask -Xml -Force; a schedule changed after apply is reported diverged and left untouched.

originalState.method: Full Export-ScheduledTask XML plus state, enabled flag, MaintenanceSettings Period/Deadline, trigger count and action command captured before the change.

sideEffects: Windows may run optimize/retrim maintenance during its idle window while the task is enabled; no forced defrag/retrim is triggered by this entry.
documentationSource: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/storage-filemanagement/defragment-optimize-your-data-drives-in-windows (Optimize Drives and its schedule; fetched 2026-11-23)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/set-scheduledtask
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/register-scheduledtask

tweaks.name: Storage Sense policy configuration
tweaks.description: Configures the documented Storage Sense policy (on/off, optional cadence) with the exact prior policy values journaled; user-data categories are never enabled.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner Windows' documented automatic space management instead of a NEXTRIX-scheduled deletion script.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxStorageSensePolicy writes only documented ADMX/CSP values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\StorageSense: AllowStorageSenseGlobal (1 allow / 0 block) and, only when the owner chooses a cadence, ConfigStorageSenseGlobalCadence (0 during low free space, 1 daily, 7 weekly, 30 monthly). Recycle-Bin and Downloads cleanup thresholds (ConfigStorageSenseRecycleBinCleanupThreshold / ConfigStorageSenseDownloadsCleanupThreshold) are never written by NEXTRIX - they delete user data and stay a user decision; they are reported if present. The documented consequence is disclosed rather than hidden: while AllowStorageSenseGlobal is configured, users cannot turn Storage Sense off in Settings, but they keep cadence control unless the cadence policy is also set - which is why the default action leaves cadence unset ('Keep'). Each layer goes through the journaled registry writer (capture -> journal -> write -> verify -> journal), so rollback restores the exact prior policy values, including absence. The per-user Settings toggle is read-only (undocumented value name, labeled E0 in the report) and is never written.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: Storage Sense policy not configured; it activates on low disk space and the user controls it in Settings.
tweaks.proposedState: AllowStorageSenseGlobal configured as chosen; cadence left to the user unless explicitly selected; prior policy state journaled.

verify.procedure: Each written policy value is re-read and must equal the requested DWord; untouched values (cadence unless requested, recycle bin/downloads thresholds) are reported as untouched with their current values.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback -TweakId NX06-004 restores every journaled policy value exactly (values that did not exist are deleted), only-if-ours.

originalState.method: Every Storage Sense policy value captured with existence, kind and data before any write; cadence and threshold values reported even when not written.

sideEffects: Documented policy lockdown: with AllowStorageSenseGlobal configured the user cannot switch Storage Sense off in Settings (rollback removes the policy). Storage Sense may delete temporary files Windows classifies as unused, and only if the user has those categories enabled.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-storage (AllowStorageSenseGlobal, ConfigStorageSenseGlobalCadence values 0/1/7/30 and registry key mapping; fetched 2026-11-23)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/configuration/storage/storage-sense (Group Policy paths and cadence choices)

tweaks.name: Temporary files cleanup (on-demand)
tweaks.description: On-demand cleanup of an explicit temporary-directory list: reports what would be deleted, deletes only with explicit consent, journals an irreversible operation record.
tweaks.objective: Reclaim temp space on request with no hidden deletion and no scheduling.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Clear-NxTemporaryFiles accepts only an explicit allow-list: a directory whose leaf name is Temp/Tmp and which lives under the Windows directory or a user profile. Drive roots, the Windows directory itself, profile roots and reparse points are refused; junctions are never followed and never deleted, so a cleanup cannot escape its roots. Enumeration is bounded (200k files) and age-gated: files written within -MinimumAgeDays (default 7) are never touched, and locked files are skipped and reported rather than forced open. The default call returns a dry-run report (roots, file count, bytes, sample names) and deletes nothing; deletion requires both -Consent and engine approval (-Approved). Before deleting, a journal 'apply' entry records the roots, threshold, planned counts and an explicit 'NOT REVERSIBLE' label; after deletion a 'verify' entry records the actual counts and per-file failures. NEXTRIX never schedules this operation and never adds wildcard sweeping: Windows' own documented mechanism for automatic temp cleanup is Storage Sense (NX06-004), which the owner controls.
tweaks.defaultState: Temp directories accumulate files until the user or Windows Storage Sense cleans them.
tweaks.proposedState: Files older than the chosen threshold under the reported temp roots deleted on explicit request; audit record journaled.

verify.procedure: Dry-run report lists accepted/refused roots, candidate count and bytes first. After a consented run the verify entry records deleted count, bytes deleted, skipped count and sample failures with the 'NOT REVERSIBLE' label.

rollback.procedure: Not reversible by design: temp-file deletion cannot be restored from the journal. The apply entry carries an explicit irreversibility label and rollback reports it as irreversible (audit record only) instead of pretending to restore.

originalState.method: Roots, age threshold, planned file count and planned bytes are journaled before deletion; individual file contents are not recoverable.

sideEffects: Deleted temp files are gone permanently; applications re-create what they need. Installer caches in %TEMP% may be removed. Open files are skipped, never forced.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-storage (AllowStorageSenseTemporaryFilesCleanup: Windows deletes user temporary files that are not in use; fetched 2026-11-23)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/configuration/storage/storage-sense (documented temp-cleanup category)

tweaks.name: Windows Update cache cleanup (on-demand)
tweaks.description: On-demand cleanup of the Windows Update download cache behind a mandatory idle gate; Windows Update is never disabled or reconfigured, and a temporary service stop requires separate explicit consent plus an unconditional restart.
tweaks.objective: Reclaim the re-downloadable update cache on request without racing an active update or weakening the update stack.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Clear-NxWindowsUpdateCache refuses to run unless Windows Update is idle: a pending reboot (WindowsUpdate RebootRequired, Component Based Servicing RebootPending, PendingFileRenameOperations), a servicing process (TiWorker, TrustedInstaller, wuauclt, MoUsoCoreWorker, SetupHost, WindowsUpdateBox) or a running wuauserv/UsoSvc/TrustedInstaller blocks it. Running services block by default; -ConsentToTemporaryServiceStop is a separate switch that allows stopping wuauserv/UsoSvc/BITS only. Services stopped this way are journaled with their exact prior status/StartType and restarted in a finally block, and the record asserts StartType unchanged - NEXTRIX never disables Windows Update, never changes a service StartType and never touches cryptsvc (the documented reset recipe stops cryptsvc; this entry deliberately does not). Deletion is narrower than the documented whole-folder reset: only files under %SystemRoot%\SoftwareDistribution\Download, age-gated and reparse-point safe. The journal records the idle verdict, service state and deletion plan before mutation, and the verify entry records deleted/skipped counts plus service restart results with an irreversible label. Never scheduled, never silent.
tweaks.defaultState: Update downloads accumulate in SoftwareDistribution\Download until Windows removes them.
tweaks.proposedState: Idle-gated deletion of download-cache files on explicit request; service state and StartType verified unchanged.

verify.procedure: Idle verdict is reported before any deletion (busy = Refused, nothing deleted). After a consented run: deleted/skipped counts, every stopped service Running again, StartType unchanged, and the irreversible label recorded in the journal.

rollback.procedure: Not reversible: deleted downloads are re-fetched by Windows Update when needed. Rollback reports the operation as irreversible (audit record only). Services are already restored by the finally block, not by rollback.

originalState.method: Idle verdict (pending reboot reasons, busy processes, service states with StartType), cache path, file count and bytes journaled before deletion.

sideEffects: Active updates are refused rather than interrupted. A consented temporary stop briefly pauses update services and they are restarted immediately; failure to restart is reported, not hidden. Downloaded updates are re-downloaded later.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/installing-updates-features-roles/additional-resources-for-windows-update (documented reset: stop wuauserv, delete %systemroot%\SoftwareDistribution, start wuauserv; NEXTRIX uses a narrower Download-only scope, an idle gate and an unconditional restart; fetched 2026-11-23)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/update/windows-update-troubleshooting (Windows Update troubleshooting hub)

tweaks.name: Delivery Optimization cache cleanup (on-demand)
tweaks.description: Deletes Delivery Optimization cached files through the documented Delete-DeliveryOptimizationCache cmdlet, preserving pinned files by default and journaling the irreversible operation.
tweaks.objective: Clear the peer-cache on request without touching Delivery Optimization policy or mode.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Clear-NxDeliveryOptimizationCache uses only the documented cmdlet Delete-DeliveryOptimizationCache: without -IncludePinnedFiles it preserves pinned content (which may be intentional, including LAN-shared content), and it never changes DODownloadMode - the Delivery Optimization mode policy is NX01-011's target. The report records cmdlet availability, active job count from Get-DeliveryOptimizationStatus and, when present, the observed cache folder size (that path is not Microsoft-documented and is labeled as observed). The function refuses nothing silently: a missing cmdlet is a reported skip. Deletion requires -Consent plus engine approval, journals an apply entry with the before-size and an explicit 'NOT REVERSIBLE' label (Microsoft documents that this deletion cannot be undone), then journals a verify entry with the after-size. Never scheduled.
tweaks.defaultState: Delivery Optimization retains cached content according to its mode (NX01-011 policy).
tweaks.proposedState: Unpinned cache content deleted on explicit request; pinned files preserved unless explicitly included; audit record journaled.

verify.procedure: Cmdlet availability and active job count are reported first; after the consented run the verify entry records the cache size before/after and the 'NOT REVERSIBLE' outcome. A missing cmdlet is reported as Skipped, never as success.

rollback.procedure: Not reversible: Microsoft documents that Delete-DeliveryOptimizationCache deletion cannot be undone. Rollback reports it as irreversible (audit record only).

originalState.method: Cache folder size, active job count and cmdlet availability journaled before deletion; content itself is not preserved.

sideEffects: Cached peer content is removed and may be re-downloaded; pinned files are kept unless explicitly included. DODownloadMode/policy is unchanged.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/deliveryoptimization/delete-deliveryoptimizationcache (default preserves pinned files; deletion cannot be undone; fetched 2026-11-23)
registry/NX01.json NX01-011 (Delivery Optimization mode policy owner - XREF, no duplicate target)

tweaks.name: NTFS last-access update policy
tweaks.description: Disables (or restores) NTFS last-access timestamp updates with the raw fsutil output and the exact persistence DWord - including the user-managed bit - journaled.
tweaks.objective: Make the last-access policy explicit and exactly reversible instead of leaving a hidden system-managed state.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxNtfsLastAccessPolicy reads fsutil behavior query disablelastaccess (which reports 'User Managed'/'System Managed' plus ENABLED/DISABLED) and the documented persistence value NtfsDisableLastAccessUpdate. That value is decoded honestly: bit 31 marks user-managed, the low bit is enabled/disabled, and system-managed modes make the effective behavior volume-dependent - which is why the report includes per-volume sizes and the raw output. Apply runs the documented fsutil behavior set disablelastaccess 1|0; verification re-queries and requires the parsed low bit to match, and the verify entry records 'Verified-RestartPending' because Microsoft documents that a restart is required. Exact rollback restores the journaled registry DWord byte-for-byte (including user-managed/system-managed encoding and value absence) before falling back to fsutil, which always re-encodes as user-managed. Microsoft documents the trade-off: backup and Remote Storage programs that rely on Last Access Time are affected. ReviOS disables last access via revitool (r2) as a configuration precedent only; no performance claim is made.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default varies: current builds often ship 'User Managed, disabled'; system-managed modes are volume-size dependent.
tweaks.proposedState: Policy disabled (or enabled) as chosen, with the exact prior DWord/absence and raw fsutil output journaled; restart pending.

verify.procedure: fsutil behavior query disablelastaccess re-parses to the requested low-bit state; registry DWord and user/system-managed flag recorded. Verification is labeled Verified-RestartPending because the effect is documented to require a restart.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx06Rollback -TweakId NX06-008 restores the exact journaled registry DWord (or deletes it when absent before apply) and only uses fsutil when that does not reproduce the recorded semantic; only-if-ours, divergence reported.

originalState.method: Raw fsutil output, parsed value plus user-managed flag, per-volume context and the exact persistence registry descriptor (existence, kind, DWord) captured before any change.

sideEffects: Backup/remote-storage tooling that relies on Last Access Time can behave differently (documented). No restart prompt is forced by NEXTRIX; the setting takes effect at the next restart.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/fsutil-behavior (disablelastaccess, NtfsDisableLastAccessUpdate mapping, restart requirement, backup-tool caveat; fetched 2026-11-23)
research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (ReviOS disables NTFS last access via revitool - precedent only)

tweaks.name: NTFS 8.3 short-name creation policy
tweaks.description: Disables (or restores) global 8.3 short-name creation with per-volume state reported first and a legacy-installer caution.
tweaks.objective: Stop new 8.3 name creation when it is not wanted, while showing exactly where short names were explicitly enabled.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Set-NxNtfs8dot3Policy reads the global registry state and, per volume, fsutil behavior query disable8dot3 <volume> (volume state, registry state, effective result). Apply runs the documented global form fsutil behavior set disable8dot3 1|0; verification re-queries the registry state and records every volume's effective state. Only creation of new short names is governed - existing short names are not removed (documented), and the function says so instead of implying a cleanup. The legacy-installer caution is stated in the entry and returned as a warning: old setup programs can depend on short names, which is why the per-volume report precedes the change. A restart is required (documented), so verification is labeled Verified-RestartPending. Exact rollback restores the journaled DWord/absence first and only falls back to fsutil if needed. ReviOS disables 8.3 via revitool (r2) as a configuration precedent only; no performance claim.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default on current images: 8.3 creation disabled on all volumes (registry state 1).
tweaks.proposedState: Global 8.3 creation policy disabled (or enabled as chosen); per-volume effective state reported; exact prior value journaled.

verify.procedure: fsutil behavior query disable8dot3 re-parses to the requested registry state; per-volume effective states are recorded. Verification is labeled Verified-RestartPending.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx06Rollback -TweakId NX06-009 restores the exact journaled registry value/absence (fsutil only if needed); only-if-ours, divergence reported.

originalState.method: Global registry state, raw fsutil output and per-volume volume/registry/effective states captured before any change.

sideEffects: Legacy installers or utilities that depend on 8.3 short names can fail after the change takes effect (documented caution). Existing short names are untouched; no space is reclaimed by this setting.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/fsutil-behavior (disable8dot3/global registry value, creation-only semantics, restart requirement; fetched 2026-11-23)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/fsutil-8dot3name (per-volume query/set form)
research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (ReviOS disables 8.3 via revitool - precedent only)

tweaks.name: NTFS memory usage configuration
tweaks.description: Reports NTFS pool-cache levels by default; the documented increased mode is an explicit-consent, preset-excluded ADVANCED choice with Microsoft's own caution disclosed.
tweaks.objective: Expose the documented NTFS pool setting honestly instead of shipping a speculative memory tweak.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: fsutil behavior query memoryusage and the documented persistence value NtfsMemoryUsage are read with memory context (total/free physical). The default action is Report: nothing is written, because Microsoft's own documentation states that raising the NTFS pool limit reduces pool memory available to other processes when the system already uses large amounts of memory and 'might reduce overall system performance'. The opt-in modes write the documented values through fsutil behavior set memoryusage 2 (increased) or 1 (default), verify the parsed value, and journal the exact persistence DWord/absence for exact restore; verification is labeled Verified-RestartPending because a restart is required. The entry is ADVANCED, preset-excluded and ExplicitConsent-gated precisely because the documented benefit is conditional and the documented risk is real. No performance claim is made in either direction.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: default NTFS pool usage (query reports 0/1 depending on build).
tweaks.proposedState: Report-only by default; increased/default pool usage only on explicit consent, with the exact prior value journaled.

verify.procedure: Report mode: current value, raw fsutil output, registry DWord and memory totals, with no mutation and no journal entry. Increased/Default mode: the parsed value and registry DWord must match the request (Verified-RestartPending).

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx06Rollback -TweakId NX06-010 restores the exact journaled registry DWord/absence (fsutil fallback only if needed); only-if-ours.

originalState.method: Raw fsutil output, parsed value, exact persistence registry descriptor and memory context captured before any write; report mode journals nothing.

sideEffects: Increasing NTFS pool memory can reduce pool memory for other processes and Microsoft warns it might reduce overall system performance; a restart is required. Report mode has no side effects.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/fsutil-behavior (memoryusage values 1/2, NtfsMemoryUsage mapping, quoted risk and restart requirement; fetched 2026-11-23)

tweaks.name: Write caching policy (per-device)
tweaks.description: Per-device write-cache policy: report by default; an explicit per-disk change journals the exact prior device value and states the power-loss trade-off.
tweaks.objective: Make the per-device cache policy visible and controllable without any blanket device sweep.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Evidence is E0 for the write path: no Microsoft document names the per-device registry value UserWriteCacheSetting, which sits in the device instance's Device Parameters\Disk key and is written by the Device Manager policy page; the documented read surface is Get-StorageAdvancedProperty (IsDeviceCacheEnabled, IsPowerProtected), which the report always includes for comparison. Default action is Report over all disks (no writes). A change requires an explicit -DiskNumber - never an all-disks sweep - plus explicit consent; the disk's PNPDeviceID from Win32_DiskDrive resolves the device instance key, and the exact prior value/absence (plus CacheIsPowerProtected if present) is journaled so rollback restores it exactly, including deleting a value NEXTRIX created. Verification is honest about its level: the registry value is re-read, while the device-level cache state may only change after re-enumeration or reboot and is reported as 'changed at read time: true/false' rather than claimed. VMs, USB bridges and RAID controllers may ignore the per-device value. The power-loss trade-off is mandatory and disclosed: acknowledged writes can be lost on power failure while caching is enabled, and disabling caching is not a power-safety guarantee.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: device cache policy is driver/OEM controlled; the user value is normally absent.
tweaks.proposedState: All disks reported by default; a named device's cache policy changed only on explicit consent, with the exact prior value/absence journaled.

verify.procedure: Report mode: per-disk registry state plus the documented IsDeviceCacheEnabled/IsPowerProtected view, no writes. Change mode: the registry value re-reads as the requested DWord, and the device-level cache state change (if any) is reported without claiming a reboot-free effect.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback -TweakId NX06-011 restores the exact journaled per-device registry value or deletes it when it did not exist; only-if-ours, divergence reported. A reboot may be required for the device to re-read the value.

originalState.method: Per-device PNPDeviceID, Device Parameters\Disk path, UserWriteCacheSetting (existence/kind/value), CacheIsPowerProtected and the documented storage-API view captured before any write.

sideEffects: POWER-LOSS TRADE-OFF: with write caching enabled, acknowledged writes may still be in the device cache when power is lost - data loss or volume corruption is possible. Disabling caching lowers throughput. Virtual machines, USB bridges and RAID controllers may ignore the value.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/storage/get-storageadvancedproperty (documented IsDeviceCacheEnabled/IsPowerProtected read surface)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntdddisk/ns-ntdddisk-_disk_cache_information (documented disk cache-mode structure behind the policy page)
E0 provenance: the registry value name UserWriteCacheSetting is community-known and written by the Device Manager policy page; Microsoft does not document it. Verified registry read-back only.

tweaks.name: Disk device power management (storage D3 in Modern Standby)
tweaks.description: Sets the documented storage D3-in-Modern-Standby policy (0 disable / 1 enable), with plan-level disk-idle settings reported as NX09 territory and never written.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner the documented storage-stack idle policy without touching plan-level power settings or sweeping per-device driver parameters.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Microsoft documents a global registry value StorageD3InModernStandby (REG_DWORD) under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Storage: 0 disables D3 support for storage devices, 1 enables it, and when the value is absent Storport follows the ACPI _DSD configuration and then the platform allowlist. Set-NxStorageD3Policy writes only that value, journaled through the registry pipeline so rollback restores the exact prior state (the value is deleted when NEXTRIX created it, which restores the documented 'unconfigured' behavior). Applicability is gated on evidence: without any S0 standby state in powercfg /a the entry skips with a reason instead of writing a value that cannot act. Boundary is explicit: plan-level disk idle timeouts (SUB_DISK DISKIDLE) belong to NX09 and are only read for the report; per-device NVMe/Storport idle parameters are reported (only if present) but never written, because blanket Enum/class power-value sweeps are on the rejected list (r1/r2) and Atlas' own power policy refuses exactly these surfaces. Trade-off stated in both directions: disabling D3 can help resume behavior at the cost of standby power/heat; enabling favours power. Verification is registry-level; the effective storage-stack behavior is applied at the next storage re-enumeration/reboot and no runtime telemetry is claimed.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: value normally not configured (Storport follows ACPI _DSD, then the platform allowlist).
tweaks.proposedState: StorageD3InModernStandby explicitly 0 or 1 as chosen, with the prior value/absence journaled; plan-level power untouched.

verify.procedure: The registry value re-reads as the requested DWord (kind DWord); the report also shows the per-disk applicability list, powercfg /a S0 evidence and the read-only plan disk-idle values. An S0-less platform is skipped, never written.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback -TweakId NX06-012 restores the exact journaled value or deletes it when absent before apply (returning to the documented 'unconfigured' state); only-if-ours, divergence reported.

originalState.method: StorageD3InModernStandby existence/kind/value, powercfg /a raw output, per-disk bus/media applicability and read-only plan disk-idle values captured before any write.

sideEffects: Latency-vs-power trade-off: disabling storage D3 keeps SATA/NVMe devices out of their deepest idle state during Modern Standby (potentially better resume behavior, higher standby power/heat); enabling D3 favours power savings. Effect applies at the next storage re-enumeration/reboot.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/configuration/wcd/wcd-storaged3inmodernstandby (documented SATA/NVMe D3 behavior in Modern Standby)
research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (Atlas power policy refuses per-device Enum power writes - boundary respected)

tweaks.name: Drive health (SMART) report
tweaks.description: Read-only health report: per-disk health/operational status plus storage reliability counters, with unsupported counters reported as unknown rather than zero.
tweaks.objective: Give owners the Windows storage stack's own health view before maintenance decisions.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxDriveHealthReport reads Get-PhysicalDisk (HealthStatus, OperationalStatus, media/bus type), Get-StorageReliabilityCounter (temperature, wear, power-on hours, start/stop and load/unload cycles, corrected/uncorrected read/write errors, latency maxima) and Get-Volume health. A per-disk verdict is derived only from documented status fields (Healthy, Warning, Unhealthy, Unknown); it is not a failure-prediction model and the report says so. Counters that the controller does not forward stay blank with the counter name listed as unavailable - blank means 'not reported', never 'zero' - because USB bridges and some RAID controllers do not expose SMART data through the storage stack. No writes, no self-tests, no firmware actions, nothing journaled.
tweaks.proposedState: A per-disk health report with reliability counters and explicit unavailability notes.

verify.procedure: Report enumerates every physical disk with health/operational status and a verdict from the documented fields; reliabilityCounterAvailable marks unsupported counters explicitly and uncertainty lists read failures.

sideEffects: None (read-only). Reliability counter queries can be slow on some controllers.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/storage/get-physicaldisk (HealthStatus/OperationalStatus)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/storage/get-storagereliabilitycounter (temperature/wear/error/latency counters)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/cimwin32prov/win32-diskdrive (device instance path used for device-scoped reports)
